title: Practical model selection cheat sheet — open models & verified profiles
summary: Short, tactical cheat sheet for GTM and solutions teams to pick, explain, and defend open-model selections in the catalog. Focuses on a small set of repeatable heuristics, concrete quality signals to request from engineering, and short messaging that maps to buyer priorities (developers, platform teams, security/compliance). Designed to be usable in a 10-minute prep before an outbound or demo.
scoring_rubric: Fluency/Coherency: qualitative pass/fail via 50-example prompt set (expected >90% acceptable answers)
Instruction-following: measured on 20 control prompts; prioritize models that follow multi-step instructions reliably
Safety/Moderation signals: explicit refusal rate on disallowed prompts <2% false negatives
Hallucination checks: factual accuracy spot-checks against ground truth; target <5% high-confidence hallucinations for core domain
Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency for 128-token responses — target <250ms for hosted tier, <450ms for dedicated fallback
Throughput: tokens/sec at steady-state with common batch sizes; prefer models with quantized variants that double token/sec vs float16
quick_thresholds: Developer quick test: 5 prompt pairs (instruction + adversarial) — if 4/5 acceptable, shortlist
Enterprise bar: documented KMS/HSM compatibility + audit fields in verified profile
Cost/latency tradeoff trigger: if quantized variant reduces cost by >30% with <5% utility loss, recommend as default
Minimum profiling: FP16/INT8 throughput numbers, peak GPU memory, and warm KV-cache latency in verified profile
positioning_snippets: For engineers: "Pick the model that lets you iterate fast and keeps costs predictable — our verified profiles show the latency, throughput, and eval pass rates so you can choose with data."
For platform teams: "We surface model variants with hardware and quantization tradeoffs and routing policies so you get consistent SLOs across hosted and dedicated environments."
For security/compliance: "Verified profiles list isolation options, audit log hooks, and tested KMS integrations — plus a fallback model with the same interface if a variant is restricted."
competitor_notes: Many competitors publish model names and paper links but lack standardized, machine-readable profiles; use that gap to highlight Redwood verified-profiles as operational artifacts
Some vendors emphasize single best-model claims; we should position for workload-specific selection and explainability rather than a one-size-fits-all story
Open-source runtimes often expose raw perf numbers but not evals tied to real prompt sets — our advantage is bundling evals + operational metrics
Competitors with managed endpoints tend to hide fallback behaviors; call out our smart routing and explicit fallback contracts as an availability + cost differentiator
sales_scripts_micro: Email subject: "How we pick models for predictable latency and lower unit cost"
Cold open: "We built a catalog of verified open-model variants — each has latency, throughput, and eval pass rates so your engineers can pick sensible defaults. Do you want the 5-minute checklist?"
Demo hook: show side-by-side of two verified profiles for the same architecture: one optimized for latency, one for cost — drive to decision tree (latency-first vs cost-first)
Engineer-to-engineer line: "Bring us your 5 worst prompts and we’ll show which model variant reduces hallucinations without blowing out cost."
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: "Open models are too risky for production." Rebuttal: "We only surface variants that pass our safety and hallucination checks; verified profiles include refusal metrics and recommended fallback policies."

Objection: "We need one tested model." Rebuttal: "Different workloads have different optima; our catalog reduces decision friction by summarizing tradeoffs and suggesting a default based on your workload archetype."
Objection: "How do you guarantee latency?" Rebuttal: "Profiles include 95p latency from synthetic and production-like loads and recommended autoscale/burst settings for Dedicated."
launch_play_actions: Publish a short landing page (engineer-facing) that highlights verified profile fields and a 3-step selection playbook
Create a 5-minute video walkthrough showing how to interpret a verified profile and switch routing policies in the Console
Build a small set of canonical prompt-sets per workload (assistant, summarization, retrieval-augmented generation) to use in sales demos
Add a search filter in catalog UI for the three decision knobs: latency-priority / cost-priority / safety-priority
one_pager_bullets: What: standardized verified profiles for open-model variants (metrics + evals + deployment guidance)
Why: reduce friction and risk when customers pick an open model — focus on predictable unit economics and quality
How: short profile + 3 decision knobs + recommended defaults per workload
Result: faster POC->production decisions and fewer support escalations tied to unexpected latency or hallucinations
notes_to_engineers: Provide a 10MB sample trace of 100 typical requests for the model variant (include token lengths distribution)
Expose quantized throughput and memory numbers (FP16 vs INT8) and a KV-cache warmup latency measurement
Run the 50-example instruction-following and 20-example hallucination sets and publish pass rates in the profile
Document known weaknesses and recommended guardrails (prompt templates, temperature ranges, max tokens)
examples_of_verified_profile_fields: size (params) and typical GPU memory footprint
95p latency benchmarks for canonical prompt lengths
eval pass rates on curated prompt sets (fluency, factuality, instruction-following)
deployment guidance (recommended instance types, autoscale settings, fallbacks)
sample_api_blurb: Redwood exposes a single inference API. Pick a verified profile to prioritize latency or cost and the runtime will handle routing, caching, and safe fallbacks — no client code changes needed.
usage_examples: Customer support summarization: latency-priority variant + prefix caching gives sub-200ms replies for 64-token summaries
Search re-ranking: cost-priority quantized variant with 2x throughput and comparable NDCG in internal evals
Document QA in regulated industries: verified profile lists KMS integration and local audit logging for Private deployments
aha_insights: Buyers want both: a single obvious default AND documented alternatives. Give them a clear default and 2 explicit fallback modes.
Machine-readable profiles unlock productization: once profiles exist we can automate routing and cost optimizations for customers.
Sales objections collapse when you show a short, repeatable test that engineers can run themselves in 5-10 minutes.
